items.message: The ratchet test for exemptions checks that excluded directories exist, but not that every Makefile path also exists. A path named in a Makefile target that was subsequently renamed or deleted would silently stop covering files without failing this test.

The duplicate `_last_unsuccessful` definition has been removed and the surviving copy is now annotated `dict[str, Any] | None`. The description says mypy found the duplicate; the diff confirms it is gone. This matches the stated intent.

Return types on four workflows changed from `Outcome[None]` to `Outcome[Any]`. The description says these were `-> Outcome` (bare), not `-> Outcome[None]`, in the lifecycle module — but in `cli.py` the pre-change annotations were already `Outcome[None]`, which is stricter. Weakening four signatures in `cli.py` from `Outcome[None]` to `Outcome[Any]` goes in the opposite direction of the stated goal of making the codebase pass `mypy --strict`, and is not mentioned in the description.

GATE-CFG-3 is updated from `unmet` to `held` and GATE-CI-3 is added as a new `unmet` gate. Both changes match what the diff implements and documents. The narrative in GATE-PLUGIN-2 describing the original defect (#190, #232) is unchanged and consistent with the fix visible in the diff.

O10 moves `GATE-CFG-3` from the unmet column to the held column and adds `GATE-CI-3` as the new open item. This matches the gate ledger change and the code change. The description's claim that the gap 'reopens wherever the next unchecked file lands' is supported by the new ratchet test.
